opening_message:
Ticket 1: Donna Ball (employee ID E024) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E024.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Full-time Payroll Specialist. Requested write access to Source Code. Full-time employees may have up to write; admin is only for the role that owns the system, so write is the maximum here. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB lists E024 as a contractor with basic training (HR note said full-time, but Security DB is authoritative for employment type). Contractors with basic training max out at read. Requested write exceeds max, so recommend granting read.
reason: Donna Ball (E024) requested write access to Source Code. According to the Security agent, the Security DB (authoritative for employment type) lists E024 as a contractor with basic security training. Contractors with basic training max out at read access (write requires advanced training; admin is never allowed for contractors). The requested write exceeds the maximum, so the maximum of read is granted. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, and E024 is a Payroll Specialist, so no admin eligibility applies.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Employee: Donna Ball (E024), requests write access to Source Code.

Two notes:
- HR agent says: role Payroll Specialist, employment type full_time, recommended write.
- Security agent says: role Payroll Specialist, employment type contractor, security training basic, recommended read. Security DB is authoritative for employment type.

Policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

Source Code is owned by Engineer role. Donna is Payroll Specialist.

If contractor with basic training: max is read. Requested write exceeds max, so grant read.

If full-time: max is write (since role doesn't own system), requested write = write, grant write.

The decision hinges on employment type. HR says full-time, Security says contractor and states Security DB is authoritative. As the Approver, I should consider which is more reliable. The Security agent says Security DB is authoritative for employment type. So contractor, basic training -> max read. Grant read.

I'll submit decision: read.
